articles.title: SoftBank races to fulfill $22.5 billion funding deal with OpenAI, sources
articles.content: STORY: SoftBank Group is reportedly racing to close a $22.5 billion funding commitment to OpenAI by the end of the year.According to sources, it's through an array of cash-raising schemes, including a sale of some investments.They added it could tap its undrawn margin loans borrowed against its valuable ownership in chip firm Arm Holdings.The bet on OpenAI is among the biggest yet by SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son.The Japanese billionaire wants to improve his firm's position in the race for artificial intelligence.To come up with the money, Son has already sold SoftBank's entire $5.8 billion stake in AI chip leader Nvidia.As well as offloading $4.8 billion of its T-Mobile stake, and slashing staff.Son has slowed other dealmaking at SoftBank's Vision Fund to a crawl.And two of the sources speaking to Reuters said any deal above $50 million now requires his explicit approval.SoftBank's push to marshal funds offers a window into the strain faced even by the world's biggest dealmakers.They're scrambling to finance ambitious AI data center projects worth hundreds of billions of dollars.SoftBank declined to comment.It secured a deal to invest in OpenAI at a $300 billion valuation in April.Since then, the valuation of OpenAI has risen dramatically.And the company is in talks to raise additional funding from investors, including Amazon.

articles.title: Nasdaq seeks to extend trading hours to nearly round-the-clock
articles.content: STORY: :: FileThe Nasdaq is seeking to roll out near round-the-clock trading of stocks.The stock exchange is one of the world’s largest and home to tech heavyweights Nvidia, Apple and Amazon.It plans to file paperwork to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to expand trading hours from 16 hours a day to 23 hours a day, five days a week.Nasdaq’s plans would see its trading week kick off on Sunday at 9 p.m. Eastern and end Friday at 8 p.m.:: FileA trading day would be split into two sessions with an hour break at 8 p.m. for maintenance, then start back up at 9 p.m., and would still feature opening and closing bells.It follows plans announced both by the New York Stock Exchange and Cboe Global Markets for those exchanges to move to nonstop five-day-a-week trading.Investor demand for nonstop trading of U.S. stocks has surged in recent years.That’s led regulators to introduce new rules and allow proposals from major exchanges to enable trading beyond traditional market hours.Today the U.S. stock market represents almost two-thirds of the market value of listed companies around the globe……and foreign holdings of U.S. equities hit $17 trillion last year, according to Nasdaq data.Advocates for moving closer to 24/7 trading argue it will allow investors, especially those outside the U.S., to react more quickly to events that happen outside regular market hours.Major Wall Street banks are cautious about the push, pointing to anxiety over lower liquidity, more volatility, and uncertainty over returns on investment.
